subject: Reseller fiscal responsibility & marketplace fee pass-through — proposed addendum language
messages:
From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@marketplaceops.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Billing Team <billing@marketplaceops.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace listing — reseller terms and fees (initial ask)

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our product team is excited about the integration. Legal asked me to confirm one point before we proceed to a partner paper: how does Redwood expect marketplace transaction fees to be handled for reseller deals routed through MarketplaceOps? Specifically: do you want these fees to be treated as pass-through costs on the Order Form (MarketplaceOps charges end customers, we reimburse) or as a deduction from Redwood payouts?

To avoid surprises for finance teams, we need a short clause for our Marketplace Addendum that clarifies fiscal responsibility and invoicing flow. Can you point me to the language you typically include, or share a redline?

I attached a blank Order Form for reference.

Best,
Amelia
Partner Programs, MarketplaceOps

Attachment: OrderForm-Example-MarketplaceOps.pdf (pdf, 128KB)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@marketplaceops.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcuss.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — reseller terms and fees (initial ask)

Amelia — thanks for flagging. Short answer: we prefer fee pass-through on the Order Form where MarketplaceOps invoiced marketplace fees are itemized and accepted by the end customer. That keeps Redwood payouts consistent and avoids us reconciling marketplace platform fees.

That said, we recognize some marketplace accounting teams insist on platform-level netting. To keep everyone comfortable, we propose two options in the addendum:

1) Pass-through approach (preferred)
- Marketplace fees charged by MarketplaceOps are listed as separate line items on the Order Form and paid by the end customer. Redwood will invoice/reserve revenue net of platform fee reimbursements only if MarketplaceOps provides timely invoice evidence.

2) Netting approach (alternate)
- MarketplaceOps may invoice Redwood for the difference between gross list price and amounts collected by the marketplace. This requires monthly reconciliation and an agreed cap on adjustments (e.g., adjustments > $5k escalate to finance).

I've drafted a short redline. Looping in Laura (legal) for precise language and Marcus (finance) for the reconciliation/cutoff thresholds.

Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redline_Reseller_Addendum_v3.docx (docx, 34KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@marketplaceops.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-30T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace listing — reseller terms and fees (initial ask)

Thanks Neha and Amelia — I reviewed the redline and made targeted edits. Main points I changed and why: 

- Clarified "Marketplace Fees" definition: included examples (transaction, distribution, platform) so there is no ambiguity.
- Added acceptance language: end customer must expressly accept line-item fees on the Order Form or via checkout record; this protects Redwood against retroactive fee allocation.
- Proof of charge: require MarketplaceOps to provide monthly detailed invoices and, for any adjustments > $2,500, include a PDF of the connected settlement report from the marketplace.
- Timing and netting: if MarketplaceOps wants Redwood to reimburse fees rather than itemizing to customers, they must: (a) provide signed monthly reconciliation; (b) obtain Redwood approval for amounts > $5k in a given month; (c) allow Redwood a 30-day dispute window.

I've attached the redline PDF and included bracketed alternatives (pass-through vs netting). My recommendation: adopt the pass-through clause as the default and retain the netting fallback only for later-stage customers who require it. That minimizes reconciliation burden for both sides.

Action items: Amelia, please confirm MarketplaceOps can supply the monthly invoice export (CSV) and settlement PDFs. Marcus, can your team confirm the $2,500/$5,000 thresholds are workable?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redline_Reseller_Addendum_v3.docx (docx, 34KB)

From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@marketplaceops.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Billing Team <billing@marketplaceops.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — reseller terms and fees (initial ask)

Laura / Neha — appreciate the clear edits. Quick responses to the action items: 

- We can provide a monthly invoice export (CSV) that includes order IDs, gross amounts, marketplace fee line items, settlement amounts, and a settlement report PDF for any adjustments. That works for our operations.
- Billing team confirms settlement PDFs are generated within 3 business days of month close.

One practical ask from our side: can Redwood accept language that permits MarketplaceOps to withhold its commission in the event of chargebacks or refunds for up to 60 days post-settlement? We want a limited holdback right so our cashflow isn't stressed by late chargebacks. We proposed 60 days with a cap of 10% of monthly gross for any single partner account.

If that cap and timebox are acceptable, we can proceed with signature and DocuSign. Otherwise, we can loop in finance for a quick sync.

Thanks — will wait for Marcus' note on thresholds and the $5k approval flow.

Amelia
Partner Programs, MarketplaceOps
